subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm planning a frog-on-a-leaf model, sketching proportions with a roughly 5cm frog body sitting atop a larger 20cm lily pad leaf lying flat, and thinking through how to extrude the leaf's outline shape.

Now I'm working out a skeleton for the frog with a spine chain from pelvis through shoulders to head, planning a sitting pose with legs spread and figuring out the positions and body radius along that spine for the sweep.

Defining body radius and color sectors...

Now I'm designing the head geometry—a broad flat shape built from a scaled sphere for the upper head, a separate flattened cream-ish lower jaw on the jaw joint, and defining the head joint position and forward-facing direction to anchor everything.

Positioning the pupils as small dark slit shapes offset toward the front-outward direction of each eye, oriented vertically to sit on the eye surface.

I'll skip the iris ring and just add a tiny white highlight spec near the eye instead. Now working out the leg structure: front legs use a shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand chain with foot targets positioned near the toe pads, defining root and target coordinates for a two-segment limb.

Setting up wrist positions and elbow bend directions...

Still wiring up toe joints and pads, then moving on to hind leg placement with hip, knee, and ankle points for the folded thigh posture.

I'm working out the knee bend direction and adjusting the ankle position slightly more extended, computing the hip-to-ankle distance to place the knee naturally forward and lateral. Then I'm fanning out the five hind toes from the ankle in a forward-outward spread.

Still placing toe geometry and pad positioning...

Now I'm thinking about thigh coloring — red-eyed tree frogs typically have blue flanks and inner thighs, so I'll add blue coloring on the inner side of the hind thigh, possibly using a banded approach along the leg sweep rather than full webbing detail, which I'll skip for simplicity.

Setting tapering radii for the limb sweeps so they thin toward the tip, then checking the belly placement so it sinks just slightly below the leaf surface to stay hidden rather than floating visibly above it.

Now I'm defining the leaf shape itself, extruding an ovate outline in the x-z plane with a sharp pointed tip, giving it smoothed curves along the sides to form a natural leaf silhouette.

Checking proportions: frog sits centered on the leaf with hind toes near z -0.05 and head around z 0.075, keeping it well within the leaf bounds. I'm adding a small pale-blue water droplet for detail, and sizing the eyes and nostrils to stay proportional to the head.

Now I'm working on skin texture, giving the lower jaw a cream color against the green body and adding a subtle mottled pattern of two lime shades for a more natural look.

For the rig, I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: arm and leg chains with contact roles, digit chains, and a spine with three joints leading up to a head joint and jaw joint. The head joint attaches to the final spine joint, positioned and oriented to connect naturally, and I'm figuring out how the hind leg's ankle and toe chains should parent correctly to the tip of the leg chain.

Toe chains parent off the leg's tip joint, with the leg chain itself rooted at the pelvis and arm chains rooted at the final spine joint. I'm also adding sweep geometry along the leg chain with varying radii, and working out how to position the toe chain's starting point relative to the leg tip.

Adding toe pads...

For eyes, I'm making a hemisphere lid cap with a limited theta range so it reads as a brow without covering the pupil's position, and checking that the pupil sphere sits slightly offset from the eye surface so it protrudes convincingly.

Working through the eye coloring — a ruby red base with a white highlight sphere offset toward the upper-right to suggest light reflection.

For the mouth, I'll pose the jaw bone rotated slightly forward to give a small open-mouth surprised expression, doing this after the jaw parts are built so rigid attachments follow the bone. I'll also add a small water droplet on the leaf, a flattened light-blue sphere rigged to the nearest bone for attachment.

Now I'm sketching thin vein rods running across the leaf surface, spaced along its length and angled outward, colored a lighter green and given a small square cross-section so they sit raised just above the leaf. Then I'm moving on to defining the frog's body sweep radius profile, figuring out how it tapers toward the head end where it meets the spine.

Defining spine chain joints...

Defining the arm limb chain...

Now I'm setting up the hind leg limb points with bend hints for the knee, plus contact points and sweep thickness for the leg geometry.

Writing toe-spreading function...
